items.title: Prompt Engineering con Copilot: construye prompts que realmente funcionen
items.description:
¿Utilizas Copilot pero no siempre obtienes los resultados que esperas?
En esta sesión práctica aprenderemos a dejar de improvisar prompts y construiremos juntos un framework sencillo para crear instrucciones más claras, efectivas y reutilizables con Microsoft Copilot.
Trabajaremos con seis elementos: contexto, objetivo, información, restricciones, resultado esperado y criterios de evaluación. A través de ejemplos y demostraciones en vivo, transformaremos prompts simples en instrucciones estructuradas que los participantes podrán reutilizar y adaptar a situaciones reales.
El objetivo no es memorizar “el prompt perfecto”, sino aprender una metodología que permita diseñar, probar y mejorar nuestros propios prompts.

items.title: Build with Copilot: De Prompts a Flujos de Trabajo Impulsados por IA
items.description:
¿Qué pasaría si Copilot pudiera convertirse en algo más que una herramienta para hacer preguntas? En esta serie práctica de seis episodios, construiremos progresivamente formas útiles de utilizar Microsoft Copilot como parte de nuestro trabajo diario. Comenzaremos diseñando mejores prompts e instrucciones reutilizables, luego utilizaremos Copilot para comprender y rediseñar procesos, estructurar ideas, analizar información, apoyar la toma de decisiones y, finalmente, crear un asistente de IA personalizado.
Cada episodio sigue un enfoque centrado en la práctica: menos teoría, más experimentación, demostraciones reales y patrones reutilizables que los participantes podrán aplicar a escenarios del mundo real.

eventOfTheSerie.description:
Todos tenemos procesos que repetimos: preparar un reporte, gestionar una solicitud, atender un requerimiento o coordinar una actividad. 

Pero antes de automatizar un proceso con IA, necesitamos entender cómo funciona y preguntarnos si realmente es la mejor forma de hacerlo. 

En esta sesión práctica utilizaremos Microsoft Copilot como compañero para analizar y rediseñar un proceso. 

A partir de un caso sencillo, construiremos prompts que nos ayuden a identificar actividades, actores, información necesaria, puntos de fricción y oportunidades de mejora.

eventOfTheSerie.description:

 En esta sesión práctica aprenderemos a diseñar un asistente de IA especializado utilizando Microsoft Copilot. Partiremos de una necesidad concreta y construiremos paso a paso su propósito, contexto, instrucciones, tareas, límites y resultados esperados.

items.title: Voice Agents Upgraded: New Speech Models and Agent Experience In Foundry
items.description:
Speech models let applications understand and generate spoken language, powering experiences like transcription, real-time voice interaction, and accessible conversational interfaces.
In this episode, we'll walk through a live demo in the Foundry playground that shows how to build, test, monitor, and optimize a voice agent from start to finish. We'll also cover the latest development in speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and speech-to-speech models in Azure Speech in Microsoft Foundry, including new MAI models, and how they make voice agents more natural and responsive.

items.title: Agents That Take Action: Secure Enterprise Integration with Azure
items.description:
An enterprise agent becomes genuinely useful when it can act on business systems. It also becomes significantly more dangerous if those integrations are not governed correctly.
In this session, we will connect our Microsoft Foundry agent to real enterprise capabilities using Azure API Management, Azure Logic Apps, Azure Functions, Azure Service Bus, OpenAPI tools, and Model Context Protocol servers.
The agent will create an incident ticket, initiate an approval workflow, invoke a protected business API, submit a long-running remediation command, and report the final result back to the user. Rather than allowing the model direct access to backend systems, we will introduce a governed integration layer with typed tool contracts, authentication, authorization, rate limiting, schema validation, retries, and centralized logging.
We will also compare the roles of OpenAPI tools, MCP servers, Logic Apps actions, Azure Functions, and asynchronous messaging. Managed identities and Microsoft Entra ID will be used to eliminate embedded API keys and apply least-privilege access across the solution.
By the end of the session, attendees will understand how to give agents meaningful enterprise capabilities without bypassing security, integration governance, or operational controls. Key topics: Microsoft Foundry tools OpenAPI and Model Context Protocol Azure API Management as an AI gateway Azure Logic Apps agent actions Azure Functions Azure Service Bus Managed identity and Microsoft Entra ID Secure and asynchronous tool execution.
This session is a part of a series, learn more here! https://aka.ms/ProBadgeSeries-TY

eventOfTheSerie.description:

Using Microsoft Foundry evaluation and observability capabilities, we will measure task completion, tool-call accuracy, groundedness, relevance, latency, safety, and operational reliability. We will trace requests across the agent, API Management, Logic Apps, Azure Functions, Service Bus, and the worker application using distributed tracing and Application Insights. 

During the live demonstration, we will deliberately introduce a faulty tool definition, observe the resulting regression, identify the cause through traces and evaluation results, correct the implementation, and apply a quality gate before releasing the updated version. 

The session will conclude with production monitoring, alerting, versioning, rollout and rollback strategies, and agent governance across multiple teams and environments. By the end of the session, attendees will know how to move from “the agent appears to work” to evidence that it is reliable, explainable, supportable, and safe to operate. 

Key topics: Microsoft Foundry evaluation Agent and tool-call quality metrics Distributed tracing Application Insights Regression testing safety and adversarial testing CI/CD quality gates Monitoring, incident response, and governance.

items.title: El día que la IA decidió trabajar en equipo (más JARVIS, menos Skynet)
items.description:
En los últimos meses hemos visto cómo la IA escribe código, genera imágenes o responde preguntas. Pero hay algo mucho más interesante ocurriendo: ¿qué pasa cuando varias IAs empiezan a trabajar juntas como un equipo real?
En esta sesión vamos a llevar esa idea a la práctica montando, desde cero, una factoría de software basada en agentes IA. Cada agente tendrá un rol claro —programador, QA, diseñador, incluso músico— y todos estarán coordinados por un agente orquestador (el “project manager” de toda la vida) que se encargará de repartir tareas, tomar decisiones y mantener el flujo de trabajo.
Lo interesante es que no será teoría: lo veremos en directo. Los agentes se comunicarán entre ellos, pasarán tareas y construirán algo real delante de nosotros. Sin guión y sin red, mostrando cómo funcionan de verdad estos sistemas cuando los pones a trabajar.
Al final tendremos un producto generado por este “enjambre” de agentes, y por el camino habremos visto cómo se diseñan, cómo colaboran y qué problemas reales aparecen cuando intentas llevar esto a la práctica.

Modern AI Apps with Azure Cosmos DB is a hands-on journey for developers and architects eager to harness the power of AI coding agents in real-world cloud app development. Each session explores how agentic workflows—where AI assists with code, design, optimization, and troubleshooting—can accelerate building, scaling, and modernizing applications on Azure Cosmos DB.
You’ll learn how to:
Go from prompt to production-ready app using agentic tools and best practices.
Design smarter data models and APIs with AI assistance.
Review, optimize, and debug code for scalability and efficiency.
Scaffold modern AI app patterns, refactor legacy code, and ensure production readiness.
Understand the evolving role of developers as AI becomes a core part of the software engineering process.
Whether you’re new to agentic development or looking to deepen your expertise, this series delivers practical guidance, live demos, and actionable insights for building the next generation of cloud-native applications.

items.title: Microsoft IQ Live
items.description:
Agents are only as good as the context they can reason over. Microsoft IQ is the intelligence layer that gives AI agents that context, spanning how your people work (Work IQ), how your business is modeled in data (Fabric IQ), your institutional knowledge and authoritative content (Foundry IQ), and fresh signal from the public web (Web IQ). Microsoft IQ Live is a bi-weekly series for developers building enterprise agents with the Microsoft IQ stack.
Across the series we explore the full stack through hands-on, demo-led sessions, grounding every concept in working code and real architectures you can adapt to your own agents. Tune in every other Thursday at 9 AM PT on Reactor.

items.title: Bring Organizational Context into GitHub to Prioritize with Confidence
items.description:
Your repositories don't live in a vacuum. Ownership, tiers, compliance status, on-call, and cost data usually already exist in your internal platform, service catalog, or CMDB, but getting that context into GitHub has meant copying it in and keeping it in sync.
This session introduces external custom properties and why they matter. We'll cover what they are, how they differ from standard custom properties, and the core value: instead of duplicating data, you reflect metadata you already own into GitHub as read-only properties, with your system staying the single source of truth. No two-way sync, no drift, no fighting over who owns the value, and it works everywhere custom properties already do: filters, selectors, and rulesets. To show it in practice, we'll walk through Port as a reference example, syncing real metadata into GitHub and putting it to work across repositories.
You'll leave understanding when to reach for external custom properties, the ownership and sync model behind them, and how partners like Port build on top of them.

items.title: From GitHub to GPU: Build an Open Source AI App with Copilot, Azure Linux, and AKS
items.description:
What does it take to turn an AI idea into a real, scalable application without hiding the infrastructure behind a black box?
We'll start with an open source GitHub repository and use GitHub Copilot to understand, adapt, and operate a complete AI workload. We deploy Ray and KubeRay on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), run LLM batch inference on an NVIDIA GPU, and explore how Azure Linux provides a lightweight, secure container host for the Kubernetes nodes under the hood.
Along the way, we'll connect the layers that make the application work using containers, Kubernetes resources, GPU scheduling, and open source operators.
We'll also explore autoscaling, network isolation, authentication, metrics, dashboards, and cost-aware management. Leave with a reusable GitHub repo and a clear roadmap for building open source AI systems on Azure.

eventOfTheSerie.title: Open-source databases for modern applications
eventOfTheSerie.description:
Modern AI applications still rely on databases. They store application data, embeddings, conversation history, and the context that powers retrieval. 

In this session, we'll explore Azure's open-source database offerings, including PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Azure DocumentDB, and discuss where each fits. 

We'll then take a deeper look at Azure HorizonDB, Microsoft's cloud-native PostgreSQL-compatible service. Through demos, you'll see how to build AI-powered retrieval workflows with vector search and AI pipelines, while gaining a practical understanding of where different open-source database technologies fit in modern application architectures.

items.title: Beyond Vibe Coding: Formal Verification for AI-Generated Software
items.description:
AI coding agents can now write substantial amounts of open-source software, but generated code still needs more than a plausible implementation and a passing test suite.
In this session, Carl will demonstrate a workflow in which AI writes code, creates a formal specification, and produces a machine-checked proof of correctness. He is applying this approach to RangeSetBlaze, an open-source Rust library, using Lean to state and prove key correctness properties.
The broader idea is language-independent: AI may make formal verification practical for ordinary software development by taking on much of the proof engineering itself. The session will explore what this workflow looks like in practice, where it works, where it breaks down, and how formal proofs can complement testing and code review as AI takes on more of the coding.

items.title: ¿Y si tu próximo agente fuera una Logic App? Conversacional, autónomo y MCP Server
items.description:
Cuando pensamos en construir agentes de IA, pensamos en frameworks, SDKs y todo el boilerplate que hay que montar antes de que el agente haga algo útil. Pero hay otro camino: Logic Apps ha incorporado el agent loop a su motor de workflows, ahora todo lo que ya tenía (conectores, ejecución durable, retries, monitorización, managed identities) se convierte en infraestructura de agentes que te viene dada.
En esta sesión, creamos en directo sobre un mismo escenario, un asistente de soporte interno, para poder compararlas bien: Parte 1, el agente conversacional. Creamos el agente desde el designer, le conectamos el modelo y le damos sus primeras tools usando conectores. Vemos cómo se depura de verdad: run history, transcripción del chat, y qué entra y sale del modelo en cada vuelta del loop. Y resolvemos el problema que casi nadie cuenta: el contexto de usuario.
Con autorización on-behalf-of, las tools dejan de ejecutarse con una cuenta de servicio y pasan a actuar con la identidad del usuario que está chateando: si el agente manda un correo, sale de tu buzón. Desplegamos el agente en Microsoft Teams. Parte 2, el agente autónomo.
Mismo escenario, pero sin nadie al otro lado: un trigger de evento arranca el workflow, el agente clasifica, decide y ejecuta por su cuenta. Vemos dónde colocar las agent actions dentro de un workflow normal, cómo combinar varias, y qué pasa con las ejecuciones de larga duración, los errores y la gobernanza cuando no hay un humano mirando.
Parte 3, la Logic App como MCP Server. Le damos la vuelta a la tortilla: en lugar de que el agente viva en Logic Apps, exponemos nuestros workflows como tools MCP para que los consuma cualquier agente externo, desde VS Code hasta el agente que tú quieras. Qué requisitos tiene que cumplir un workflow para ser una tool, cómo se gestionan las API keys y cómo montar varios MCP Servers en una misma Logic App.
Además, hablaremos sobre decisiones de arquitectura: Consumption con modelo gestionado por Microsoft o Standard trayendo tu propio modelo de Foundry, con sus diferencias en redes, autenticación, billing y desarrollo local. Si vienes del mundo pro-code, esta sesión te va a sorprender: no se trata de elegir entre código o designer, sino de saber cuándo el motor de Logic Apps te ahorra construir la mitad de tu plataforma de agentes.
Key Takeaways: Cómo construir agentes conversacionales y autónomos con el agent loop de Logic Apps, y en qué se diferencian Cómo ejecutar tools con la identidad real del usuario mediante autorización on-behalf-of Cómo desplegar tu agente en Microsoft Teams para que hable donde ya están tus usuarios Cómo exponer workflows como MCP Servers remotos consumibles desde cualquier agente o cliente MCP Consumption o Standard: qué SKU elegir según modelo, redes, billing y compliance.

items.title: Episode 1 | 더 스마트한 AI 워크플로 설계
items.description:
세션 소개

items.title: AI Genius | Season 6
items.description:
AI 워크플로 구축을 넘어, 한 단계 더 나아가세요.
Microsoft AI Genius Series란?
Microsoft AI Genius Series는 AI 아이디어를 실제 프로덕션 환경에서 작동하는 솔루션으로 발전시키고 싶은 개발자를 위한 프로그램입니다.
지난 시즌에는 실습 중심의 과정을 통해 Microsoft와 GitHub 기술을 활용한 AI 애플리케이션 개발부터 실제 환경 배포까지의 전 과정을 경험했습니다.
Season 6, 무엇이 달라졌을까요?
Season 6에서는 AI 워크플로를 구축하는 단계를 넘어, 더 효율적인 에이전트 경험을 설계하고 품질을 지속적으로 측정하며 프로덕션 환경에서 안정적으로 운영하는 방법을 배웁니다.
GitHub Copilot, Azure AI Foundry와 최신 AI 플랫폼 기능을 활용해 설계(Architect) → 측정(Measure) → 운영(Operate)으로 이어지는 과정을 경험하며, 대규모 환경에서도 효율적이고 안정적으로 운영되는 AI 시스템을 구현하는 역량을 키울 수 있습니다.
이번 시즌은 AI를 설계하고, 측정하고, 운영하는 세 단계의 실전 여정으로 이어집니다.
- Episode 1 | 더 스마트한 AI 워크플로 설계
비주얼 오케스트레이션, 토큰 최적화, 컨텍스트 엔지니어링, 확장 가능한 에이전트 기능을 활용해 효율적인 멀티 에이전트 워크플로를 설계하는 방법을 알아봅니다.
- Episode 2 | AI 워크플로 품질 측정, 벤치마킹 및 개선
Azure AI Foundry의 평가 프레임워크와 Intelligence Quality(IQ), Evaluations, Agent Optimiser를 활용해 성능을 벤치마킹하고 품질, 속도, 비용 간의 균형을 최적화하는 방법을 살펴봅니다. 또한 지속적인 평가를 통해 성능 저하를 방지하는 방법을 알아봅니다.
- Episode 3 | 레거시 현대화에서 AI 운영까지
자가 복구 에이전트와 엔터프라이즈급 운영 인텔리전스를 활용해 애플리케이션을 현대화하고 AI 시스템을 대규모로 안정적으로 운영하는 방법을 알아봅니다. 프로덕션 시스템을 모니터링하고 문제 해결을 가속화하며 AI 기반 운영을 효과적으로 확장하는 방법도 살펴봅니다.

3.	Azure SRE Agent를 활용해 문제를 진단하고, 검증된 해결 방안을 제안하는 방법
4.	토큰 효율성, 복구 시간, 승인 신호를 활용해 운영 효과를 추적하는 방법

items.title: Microsoft AI Genius 第六季
items.description:
你正在成为下一个 AI 高手，所以你的目标当然不只是构建 AI 工作流。你还希望让它们更高效、可衡量，并且能够在规模化应用中保持稳定与韧性。
那么，Microsoft AI Genius Series 正是帮助你迈向下一阶段的理想选择。
什么是 Microsoft AI Genius Series？
Microsoft AI Genius Series 是一项面向开发者的系列活动，旨在帮助开发者将 AI 技术从概念转化为真正可投入生产环境的解决方案。
在之前的多个 Season 中，亚洲各地的开发者通过实操式学习，借助 Microsoft 和 GitHub 技术，学习如何使用 AI 技术进行编码、构建应用并将其真正落地。
Season 6 有哪些新内容？
Season 6 将进一步从构建 AI 工作流走向规模化优化与运营 AI 工作流，带你了解如何设计更高效的 Agent 体验、持续衡量 AI 工作流质量，并在生产环境中构建和运行更具韧性的 AI 系统。
本季将借助智能 GitHub Copilot 副驾驶® 、Microsoft Foundry（国际版）以及现代 AI 平台能力，围绕架构设计（Architect）→ 衡量评估（Measure）→ 规模化运营（Operate） 三个阶段展开。
本季包含三场注重实践与动手体验的课程：
Episode 1｜通过可视化编排、Token 优化和可扩展的 Agent 能力，设计更智能的 AI 工作流
学习如何利用可视化编排、Token 优化、上下文工程和可扩展 Agent 能力，构建更加高效的多 Agent 工作流。
Episode 2｜利用 Microsoft IQ、Evaluations 和 Agent Optimizer 衡量、评测并持续优化 Microsoft Foundry AI Agents

Episode 3｜从legacy应用现代化到 AI 运维：借助自愈型 Agent 与企业级运维智能，实现应用现代化与 AI 系统规模化运营
探索自愈型 Agent、自动化现代化升级和运维智能，了解如何持续监控生产系统、加速问题修复，并更有信心地规模化开展 AI 驱动的运营。
立即开始，开启你的 AI Genius 进阶之旅  ⬇️

eventOfTheSerie.title: 利用 Microsoft IQ、Evaluations 和 Agent Optimizer 衡量、评测并持续优化 Microsoft Foundry AI Agents
eventOfTheSerie.description:
**课程介绍** 

构建 AI Agent 只是第一步。要让 Agent 从一开始就表现出色，需要为其提供高质量的上下文；而当 Agent 正式投入使用后，如何持续保持良好表现，则是一项长期工作。这包括通过评测持续监控质量、通过优化控制成本，以及通过可靠的方法判断每一次调整是否真正带来了改进。 

本场课程将介绍如何利用 **Microsoft Foundry（国际版）、Evaluations 和 Agent Optimizer 衡量** 、评测并持续优化 AI 工作流质量，以及如何借助 **Microsoft IQ** 为 Agent 提供高质量的上下文。你还将了解如何通过持续评测，用可衡量的信号取代主观判断，在 Agent 的整个生命周期中持续监控并优化其表现。 

**你将学到** 

・如何使用 **Microsoft Foundry** 对不同模型进行比较和选择 
・如何为 Agent 添加组织上下文 
・如何为 Agent 构建持续评测 Pipeline 
・如何评估和平衡质量、速度与 Token 成本 
・如何使用 **Agent Optimizer** 持续优化 Agent 
・如何在 **CI/CD Pipeline** 中管理 Agent 

**涉及技术**

・Microsoft Foundry 
・Microsoft Foundry Extension for Visual Studio Code 
・Microsoft Foundry Evaluations 和 Agent Optimizer 
・GitHub Actions，与 Microsoft Foundry 进行集成 

**适合人群** 

・希望使用 **Microsoft Foundry** 构建、评测和优化 Agent 的开发者及技术人员 
・希望将 Agent 引入 **GitHub 和 CI/CD 流程**的团队

规模化实现legacy应用现代化只是整个转型旅程的一半。随之而来的 AI 系统还需要持续监控、快速响应故障，并保障日常稳定运行，同时尽可能减少额外的工程负担。

**你将学到** 

・如何使用 Copilot Modernize CLI，规模化开展legacy应用评估与升级 
・如何利用堆叠式拉取请求，让大规模自动化迁移更易于审查 
・如何借助 Azure SRE Agent 诊断问题，并提出经过测试验证的修复方案 
・如何通过 Token 效率、恢复时间和接受度信号，衡量和追踪实际运维成效 

**涉及技术** 

・Azure SRE Agent 
・Copilot App Modernization Agent & Modernize CLI 
・Stacked Pull Requests 
・Human-in-the-Loop Governance Patterns 

**适合人群** 

・需要跨多个代码仓库推进legacy应用现代化的团队 
・负责生产环境 AI 系统运行的开发者和平台工程师

items.description:
セッションの紹介
AIエージェントの活用が大規模化・高度化する中、効率的なコンテキスト管理とビジュアルオーケストレーションは、次世代のAI開発を支える重要な要素となっています。

実践的なデモを通じて、複数のAIエージェントを連携する方法や、コンテキスト管理を最適化するアプローチ、さらにはチャット中心の操作からビジュアルオーケストレーションへと進化する新たな開発体験をご覧いただけます。
学習内容
• GitHub Copilot の Canvases を活用し、複数のAIエージェントが連携する複雑な開発を効率的に進めるための、ビジュアルワークスペースの活用方法

items.title: AI Genius | Operate & Scale: Self-Healing ZeroOps and Enterprise-Wide Modernization​
items.description:
From legacy modernization to AI operations: Modernize applications and operate AI systems at scale with self-healing agents and enterprise-grade operational intelligence
Session Introduction
Modernizing legacy applications at scale is only half the journey — the AI systems that follow demand continuous monitoring, rapid incident response, and dependable day-to-day operations, all without adding engineering burden.
In this session, you’ll follow that path end to end: modernize legacy applications with automated, reviewable upgrades, then operate and scale AI systems using self-healing agents and enterprise-grade operational intelligence. You’ll see how AI can streamline large-scale application updates, connect runtime signals to remediation, and make complex operational work easier to review and govern.
You Will Learn
• How to scale legacy application assessments and upgrades with Copilot Modernize CLI
• How stacked pull requests can make large automated migrations easier to review
• How the Azure SRE Agent can help diagnose issues and propose tested remediations
• How to track operational impact using token efficiency, recovery time, and acceptance signals
Technologies Used
• Azure SRE Agent
• Copilot App Modernization Agent & Modernize CLI
• Stacked Pull Requests
• Human-in-the-Loop Governance Patterns
Who Should Attend
• Teams modernizing legacy applications across multiple repositories
• Developers and platform engineers operating AI systems in production
• Site reliability and DevOps teams exploring agent-assisted remediation
• Technology leaders focused on scalable, resilient AI operations

items.description:

规模化实现legacy应用现代化只是整个转型旅程的一半。随之而来的 AI 系统还需要持续监控、快速响应故障，并保障日常稳定运行，同时尽可能减少额外的工程负担。

你将了解 AI 技术如何简化大规模应用更新，将运行时信号与问题修复相连接，并让复杂的运维工作更加易于审查和治理。
你将学到
・如何使用 Copilot Modernize CLI，规模化开展legacy应用评估与升级
・如何利用堆叠式拉取请求，让大规模自动化迁移更易于审查
・如何借助 Azure SRE Agent 诊断问题，并提出经过测试验证的修复方案
・如何通过 Token 效率、恢复时间和接受度信号，衡量和追踪实际运维成效
涉及技术
・Azure SRE Agent
・Copilot App Modernization Agent & Modernize CLI
・Stacked Pull Requests
・Human-in-the-Loop Governance Patterns

・需要跨多个代码仓库推进legacy应用现代化的团队

セッションの紹介
レガシー・アプリケーションの大規模なモダナイゼーションは、変革の第一歩に過ぎません。AIシステムを本番環境で安定的に運用するためには、継続的な監視、迅速な障害対応、そして高い信頼性を実現するための仕組みが不可欠です。

学習内容
• Copilot Modernize CLI を活用し、複数のレガシーアプリケーションの評価やアップグレードを効率的に展開する方法　
• Stacked Pull Requests を活用し、大規模な自動マイグレーションのレビューを効率化する手法　
• Azure SRE Agent を活用し、問題の診断や検証済みの修復策を提案する方法
• トークン効率、復旧時間、受け入れ率などの指標を用いて、運用効果を可視化・追跡する方法
使用技術
•Azure SRE Agent
• Copilot App Modernization Agent & Modernize CLI Stacked Pull Requests
• Human-in-the-Loop ガバナンスパターン
こんな方におすすめ
• 複数のリポジトリにまたがるレガシーアプリケーションのモダナイゼーションに取り組んでいるチーム　
• 本番環境でAIシステムを運用する開発者やプラットフォームエンジニア
• エージェント支援による障害対応や運用改善を検討しているSRE・DevOpsチーム

items.title: Toma mejores decisiones con Copilot: de la información a la acción
items.description:
En esta sesión práctica aprenderemos a utilizar Microsoft Copilot como apoyo para estructurar y analizar decisiones, construyendo juntos un framework sencillo que nos permita evaluar alternativas de manera más clara y consciente.
Trabajaremos con seis elementos: problema, evidencia, alternativas, criterios, riesgos y recomendación. A través de ejemplos y demostraciones en vivo, utilizaremos Copilot para organizar información, comparar opciones, identificar supuestos y explorar riesgos antes de tomar una decisión.
El objetivo no es que Copilot decida por nosotros, sino aprender una metodología que nos permita analizar, cuestionar y tomar decisiones mejor informadas manteniendo el criterio y la responsabilidad humana.

items.title: AI-Assisted Linux Operations on Azure: Deploy, Observe, Troubleshoot
items.description:
AI on Linux is only part of the story.
In this demo-led session, Karl Abbott explores how AI can assist with operating Linux environments on Azure.
Join this demo-led session exploring AI-assisted Linux operations on Azure.

Leave with practical ideas for bringing AI into day-to-day Linux operations, from deployment and observability to troubleshooting.

items.title: Construye tu forma de trabajar con Copilot: integra la IA en tu día a día
items.description:
En esta sesión práctica aprenderemos a conectar diferentes formas de utilizar Microsoft Copilot y construiremos juntos un framework sencillo para diseñar una forma de trabajo potenciada por IA, desde una necesidad hasta un resultado concreto.
Trabajaremos con seis elementos: necesidad, prompt, proceso, asistente, decisión y resultado. A través de ejemplos y demostraciones en vivo, integraremos lo aprendido durante la serie para diseñar un flujo de trabajo en el que Copilot pueda ayudarnos a analizar información, ejecutar tareas, estructurar ideas y apoyar decisiones.
El objetivo no es utilizar IA en cada actividad, sino aprender una metodología que permita identificar dónde Copilot aporta valor, cómo integrarlo de manera consciente y cómo construir una forma de trabajo que podamos probar, mejorar y adaptar a nuestras propias necesidades.

speakers.name: Jenny Ferries
speakers.title: Principal Software Engineering Manager
speakers.bio:
I'm a Principal Software Engineering Manager in CoreAI’s 1ES division at Microsoft, leading an AI-Native Engineering team, a pioneering group shaping the next generation of how humans and AI build software together.In this charter role, I will architect and scale new paradigms for AI-human collaboration and agentic workflows, tackling high-priority business and security challenges while setting global benchmarks for developer productivity and AI partnership. My focus spans co-creative engineering practices, rapid prototyping, large-scale codebase modernization, and making AI a trusted teammate—not just a tool—across the software lifecycle.

Previously, I led the transformation of Microsoft’s Entra authentication SDKs (7 trillion+ requests daily), guiding my team and product toward AI-native approaches that reduced developer toil and unlocked new value for internal and external customers.My passion is helping teams move beyond prompt engineering—establishing cultures where engineers and AI agents work side by side as thinking partners and co-creators. 

I came to Microsoft through the LEAP program, leaving a successful 14 year career as a teacher, read more about my journey here: https://news.microsoft.com/life/the-evolution-of-a-passion/
